Subject: PO vs Card — procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Use case: internal search + generative summaries for support tickets (lowish token volumes to start, potential to scale).
- Procurement: AP prefers purchase orders (POs). Team indicated vendor onboarding and security questionnaire steps are required before procurement can start.
- Commercial path: you asked about using credit card for POC vs PO for production, and whether we support marketplace billing.

Next steps / asks from our side:
1) Could you confirm the AP contact and a rough timeline for vendor onboarding?
2) If PO is mandatory, do you have a standard terms or PO template we should expect?
3) Are you interested in trying a short POC on a credit card to move faster, while we run the vendor onboarding in parallel?

I attached a short vendor packet with our standard procurement details and a draft SOW to speed review. I’ve cc'd Marissa to help with anything specific on the procurement path and marketplace options.

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call with your AP team if useful.

Best,

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- AP contact: I've looped in Marcus (cc'd). He owns vendor onboarding and contracts.
- Timeline: vendor onboarding + security review is usually 3–6 weeks for us (depends on SOC 2 evidence and paperwork).
- Payment method: our policy prefers PO for production spend over $10k/year; for short POCs under $5k we can usually pay by credit card.
- Marketplace: we prefer AWS Marketplace for recurring procurement when available because it simplifies billing and internal approvals, but we're open to direct vendor contracts if necessary.

Two asks: can you confirm the exact SOC 2 artifacts you can provide, and whether Redwood is available via AWS Marketplace or plan to be? Also, Marcus — can you share any vendor setup forms or a PO template?

Thanks,
Sophie
Director of Product Operations, FinOpsCo

Hi Sophie / Marcus —

Great context, thanks. Quick answers:

- SOC 2: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a short security summary (controls matrix). Marissa, I’m cc'ing you to drop the links and any additional evidence.
- AWS Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace with private offers for enterprise customers. We can do the POC on a credit card while we set up your formal procurement through AWS Marketplace or a direct PO (your preference).
- Vendor onboarding: common items required are W9, company address, primary contact, and the SOC 2 report. If you have a vendor setup form, we can return a completed packet within 48 hours once we have the form.

Attached: redwood_vendor_packet.pdf (includes W9, company info, standard master services agreement highlights) and SOW-draft.docx (PO-friendly statement of work).

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus: if you can share your vendor setup form and PO template, we’ll fill it out and return within 48 hours.
- Sophie: decide whether you'd prefer a fast POC on card (budget under $5k) vs holding for PO + Marketplace billing.
- Marissa / Redwood procurement: coordinate to confirm SOC 2 link and marketplace SKU / private offer details.

I can also schedule a 30-minute call next week with Marcus + our procurement lead if that helps unblock timelines.

Best,
Aditya

Hi Marcus / Sophie —

Thanks for the details — I work on procurement/customer ops at Redwood and will own vendor onboarding. A few notes to make this practical: 

1) SOC 2 evidence: here's a link to our secure doc portal (SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf). I'll send an access link to Marcus directly.
2) Marketplace: we have an AWS Marketplace SKU and can do a private offer. That route typically shortens legal review because it uses marketplace terms, but it still needs a PO from your side for purchase orders.
3) Vendor form: Marcus, please send the vendor setup form. We will complete and return within 48 hours. 
4) Timeline expectations: if you share your vendor form and PO template today, a typical completion + approval for PO billing is 2–3 weeks (assuming no unusual legal redlines). If you prefer the card-PO hybrid approach (PO for long-run, card for POC), we can support that — we recommend a short card POC so you can validate model quality while onboarding.

Action items: 
- Marcus: send vendor onboarding form + PO template (target: EOD Tue 15 Jun).
- Sophie: let us know decision on POC card vs waiting for PO (target: Tue 15 Jun).
- Aditya: schedule a 30-min sync with Marcus if Marcus prefers a walk-through of onboarding fields.

Happy to jump on a call next week — I’ll propose some times if I don’t hear back.
